questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Quality of the institution

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, because Seoul National University was not helpful at all for exchange students, and you were left mostly to your own devices.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: SNU did plan an orientation for exchange students, but the number of students allowed was minimal, and it was sold out within 24 hours, and we did not receive further help, other than emails before our stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was several options of dorms to apply for, however getting them were based on luck. I am not sure about the chances.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cafeterias

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is cheap and comfortable at the global building, however I've heard worse about the older buildings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: SNU has a very confusing registration process for the classes, but it ultimately allows for a lot of time to register, however classes in English are very limited, so therefore understanding the process to begin with is important.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails with guidance

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not very successful, due to the confusion of the class registration, however I did manage to find good classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the e-mail through well, and also talk with other students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The professors had a lot of freedom to create their courses, and the Korean professors in my case were absolutely amazing professors, and I was very happy with the academic level. However one single professor was not that good, so perhaps it is also about luck.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professors obviously had a lot more freedom to change and shape their courses to their own liking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Queer Literature
Religion and identity in East Asia
Korean Literature and Korean society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Queer Literature had an amazing professor, who I absolutely would recommend. The professor of Korean Literature and Korean Society was also good, however his style may not fit everyone.

questions.answer: The Korean Healthcare system had increased their prices.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The club activities at SNU are more limited, and their festival budget is not as big as other universities, however SNU is known for this, and I recommend going to SNU for their academic level, if that is where your priorities are.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the other cities. Especially Busan and Jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining Korean classes if possible, if not then speak with the Koreans in your classes. Besides this, bars and clubs are the only other options I know of.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fashion and general aesthetics are amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You should go to SNU for their high academic level. They don't provide much for exchange students besides this.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The classes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Attending classes in Korean.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
